agency: Port Meridian Department of Building Safety

target_fields.permit_id: The permit application number assigned to the permit, not the partner's internal row identifier.
target_fields.permit_type: The numeric permit type code from 1 to 8 as listed in the agency's code table.
target_fields.filed_date: The date the application was filed, in YYYY-MM-DD format, not the date the record was created in the partner's system.
target_fields.issued_date: The date the permit was issued, in YYYY-MM-DD format, not the date the plans were approved.
target_fields.completed_date: The date the work was signed off as complete, in YYYY-MM-DD format, blank while the work is not complete, and not the date the status last changed.
target_fields.street_number: The street number of the work site.
target_fields.street_name: The street name of the work site followed by its street suffix abbreviation.
target_fields.zipcode: The five-digit ZIP code of the work site.
target_fields.estimated_cost: The cost estimated on the application, in whole US dollars, not the revised cost after plan review.
target_fields.revised_cost: The revised cost after plan review, in whole US dollars, not the cost originally estimated on the application.
target_fields.existing_stories: The number of storeys of the building before the work, in storeys rather than dwelling units.
target_fields.proposed_stories: The number of storeys of the building after the work, in storeys rather than dwelling units.
target_fields.existing_use: The current use of the building before the work.
target_fields.proposed_use: The use of the building after the work.
target_fields.description: The free-text description of the work.

transforms.identity: The column already holds the field in target format, so it is used unchanged.
transforms.date_mdy: The column holds a month/day/year text date that must be converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.date_dmy: The column holds a day/month/year text date that must be converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.date_yyyymmdd: The column holds an 8-digit YYYYMMDD date that must be converted to YYYY-MM-DD.
transforms.cents_to_dollars: The column holds an amount in cents that must be divided by 100 to obtain whole US dollars.
transforms.thousands_to_dollars: The column holds an amount in thousands of dollars that must be multiplied by 1000 to obtain whole US dollars.
transforms.decode_codelist: The column holds a letter code that must be translated through the code list in that source's dictionary into a permit type name and then to its numeric code.
transforms.type_name_to_code: The column holds a permit type name that must be translated to its numeric code with the code table.
transforms.address_number: The street number must be taken from a combined site-address column.
transforms.address_street: The street name and suffix must be taken from a combined site-address column.

pair_col_desc: See the note below this table for the exact meaning of this column.
date_pair_note: Columns {a} and {b} hold the {f1} and the {f2}, but the partner did not document which is which.
errata_swap: The dictionary descriptions of columns {a} and {b} were exchanged by mistake, so each column holds what is described under the other.
errata_unit: Since release {release}, column {col} is exported in {unit}, whatever its description above says.
errata_rename: Column {old} is now named {new} in the export file; its description above is unchanged.
schema_header: Every source must be mapped to all of the target fields below. Dates are given as YYYY-MM-DD and amounts are in whole US dollars; the permit type code table and the transform menu follow.
intro: {agency} receives building-permit exports from partner organisations: {n} sources, {first} through {last}. Each source is a partner export with its own column names, a data dictionary and sample rows. For every source and every target field, find the source column holding that field (or null if none) and the transform from the menu. Dictionaries may contain notes and errata that override the table; columns can be renamed, mislabelled, or look like a target field without being one; and some questions, such as which date is which or whether the date order is day/month, can only be settled by looking at the values. Every source is graded separately, and a source counts only if all of its fields are right.
answer_line: Your final answer is one JSON object mapping every source id to an object that has every target field as a key, with each value either null or a two-element list [column name, transform name], for example {example}.

tools.read_target_schema: Show the target fields, the permit type code table and the transform menu.
tools.list_sources: List the sources as id | partner | columns | rows, paged with an offset and a limit.
tools.read_dictionary: Show one source's data dictionary together with its notes and errata.
tools.read_rows: Show CSV rows of one source with the export header, using an offset and a limit of up to 15.
tools.column_profile: Profile one column of one source: blanks, distinct values, min, max and examples.

unit_prompt: Map only source {src}. Use read_target_schema, read_dictionary, read_rows and column_profile to inspect it, apply any notes and errata (which override the dictionary table), resolve renamed or mislabelled columns and confirm ambiguous dates and units against the actual values, then map every target field to null or to [column, transform]. End with exactly one final line of the literal form: UNIT | {src2} | <JSON object mapping every target field to null or [column, transform]>.
